title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
why: A systematic study of harness design for long-horizon self-evolving autoresearch agents, isolating context management (what is retained from past attempts) and skill management (how lessons are stored and reused), then combining the winning choices in MLEvolver. Directly in scope as retained non-weight harness components for self-evolving agents, compared with AIDE and OpenEvolve.
mechanism: Within a shared agent framework, context folding keeps individually accessible records of past attempts, and skill management selectively deletes persistently unused lessons rather than consolidating them or promoting them to standing rules. MLEvolver combines context folding and skill deletion so that accumulated experiment history and curated skills persist into later runs.
evaluation_signal: Authors report, with gpt-oss-120b, gpt-6-luna, and gpt-6-sol on MLE-Bench and KernelBench, that context folding beats a recency-truncation baseline in all six settings (up to 19.2%). Combined MLEvolver is reported to reach a 72.7% medal rate on MLE-Bench Lite and a 94% fast_1 score on KernelBench Level 3, substantially outperforming AIDE and OpenEvolve under the same inference budget.

title: Improving the Improver: Semantic PID Control for Medical Agent Self-Improvement
why: Focuses on improving the improver itself: Semantic PID-RSI is a control-theoretic framework that selects and adopts batches of modifications to a medical agent workflow (CliAgent) under noisy clinical feedback, with staged probing and independent adoption judging. In scope as RSI over a retained non-weight agent workflow, including the improvement policy.
mechanism: The improver scores candidate modification batches with three diagnostic roles inspired by PID control (P isolates current failure modes, I synthesizes evidence from past trials, D estimates response dynamics and regression risk). Selected plans are compiled into behavior contracts, then staged-probed and independently judged for adoption into the CliAgent workflow.
evaluation_signal: Authors report that evolving CliAgent with Semantic PID-RSI on a 3B-activated open-weight model yields gains of up to +6.27 C-index points on oncology pT/pN staging and survival prognosis, outperforming overfitting-prone RSI baselines and approaching frontier proprietary models that use the same CliAgent workflow.

title: AutoSECO: Automated Skill Evolution for Cross-Problem Combinatorial Optimization with General-Purpose LLM Agents
why: Evolves a reusable solver-development skill from execution feedback and retains a revision only when a fresh solver developed under the revised skill improves on a held-out evaluation gap. The frozen skill then transfers to new CO problems and to other model-harness setups. In scope as skill-library evolution with an explicit retain/rollback rule.
mechanism: Performance shortfalls of a completed solver are traced through solver code and recorded development decisions to deficiencies in the guidance skill. Revisions are written as general instructions and kept only if a newly developed solver under the revised skill achieves a lower mean evaluation gap. Evolution is run only on TSP; the resulting skill is then frozen.
evaluation_signal: Authors report a final mean TSP benchmark gap of 0.52% versus 0.98% for the SkillOpt skill-evolution baseline. Evolved only on TSP, the frozen skill is reported to improve aggregate results on capacitated vehicle routing, job-shop scheduling, and 3D bin packing relative to no skill, the initial skill, and SkillOpt, and to remain useful under alternative model-harness configurations.

title: Self-Evolving Evaluation Environments for Computer-Use Agents
why: CUA-SEE is a closed-loop evaluation environment that co-evolves tasks and executable verifiers from rollout evidence, with separate objectives for benchmark growth, diagnostic probes, and verifier precision. In scope as co-evolving evaluators/curricula for computer-use agents, a counterpart to self-evolving agents.
mechanism: Three coupled evolution loops: benchmark evolution expands scope via cohort-calibrated difficulty and coverage; diagnostic evolution adds agent-conditional capability-boundary probes; verifier evolution turns changing requirements into state-grounded checkpoints with adversarial validation. Tasks and verifiers are retained as the evaluation environment for later rounds.
evaluation_signal: Authors report that, across multiple agents, applications, and rounds, CUA-SEE generates challenging measurable tasks while preserving process-level evidence, and position adaptive evaluation as a scalable counterpart to self-evolving agents. The abstract does not quote a single headline metric.

title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
why: A dual-agent robotic-manipulation framework that refines the execution harness (hierarchical memory and operational guidance) from execution evidence without updating model parameters, including a recursive harness self-improvement step across attempts. In scope as harness-level RSI with frozen VLMs.
mechanism: An Actor interacts with the robot-control interface while a Reflector turns execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical memory keeps short-term context and long-term experiential knowledge. Evidence-based reflection diagnoses failures from observed interactions, and Recursive Harness Self-Improvement refines operational guidance across successive attempts; model weights stay frozen.
evaluation_signal: Authors report success rates of 82.4%, 76.7%, and 94.4% on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboSPA, and RMBench, and a 96.7% average success rate across three real-world manipulation tasks.

title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
why: A benchmark that measures one agent's self-improvement across episodes with fixed weights, using three views on the same run (knowledge, whether the agent's own evidence supports it, and task progress) in a world that resets while only the agent's knowledge carries over. In scope as an audit/benchmark of self-improving agents.
mechanism: Built on Outer Wilds: each episode is a 22-minute loop after which the world resets and only the agent's knowledge persists. After every episode the benchmark records places reached and ship-log facts, accuracy on 164 world questions, and whether each answer is supported by frames and positions the agent cites from its own recorded play, checked by two LLM judges from different model families.
evaluation_signal: Authors report that in eight-episode baselines with GPT-6.1 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon planners the three views do not move together. The GPT-6.1 Sol agent's correct answers are reported to grow from 14.6% to 26.8% of all questions by episode 8; the abstract presents this as evidence that any single view is an incomplete picture of improvement.

title: Blind to What They Can Fix: A Detection Gap in Self-Improving Agents
why: An audit of self-improving agents that rewrite task programs from execution feedback (a form of RSI): after agents reach high scores, the runtime checks they were told to write stay silent on many failures when the environment changes, even though those failures can be detected and then repaired. In scope as a negative-result audit of self-improving agents.
mechanism: Agents write programs that run a task without calling a model at every step, then improve those programs by running them, studying failures, and revising the code. The study asks whether the same process also yields trustworthy runtime checks, and compares author-written checks with a monitor built from records of normal runs and with a second pass in which the same agents are called to repair detected failures.
evaluation_signal: Authors report that in five task domains with up to seven author models, programs reach high scores, yet when the environment changes the checks stay silent on half or more of the resulting failures in four domains. A monitor built from records of normal runs catches most of them in three domains, and the same agents usually repair them once called. They argue that evaluations of self-improvement should measure whether a system notices its own failures, not only scores.

title: DoppelVet: Comparative Safety Verification for Self-Evolving Agents
why: A pre-retention verification framework for self-evolving agents that store feedback as reusable memories or skills: DoppelVet constructs a matched alternative update, replays both from the same state, and compares behaviors before deciding whether to keep the candidate. In scope as an audit/gate for retained non-weight updates.
mechanism: Without safety labels, DoppelVet builds an alternative update that matches every signal used by the existing verifier, replays both updates from the same state in both presentation orders, and only then decides whether the candidate may enter persistent memory or skills (evaluated on executable programs and natural-language memories).
evaluation_signal: Authors report that across nine open-weight and proprietary verifiers, mean harmful-update detection AUC rises from 0.762 to 0.940 on DoppelVet-Grid and from 0.681 to 0.826 on DoppelVet-Tool, outperforming VaG and AgentDoG 1.5. On DoppelVet-Grid, trajectories experiencing degradation over a ten-generation self-update loop fall from 30.39% to 0.43%, with no final degradation.

title: Self-Evolving Beyond Human-Crafted Experience for EDA Scripting
why: ZhuLong-SE adds governed cross-task self-evolution on top of a task-level EDA scripting harness: execution traces are distilled into a three-tier memory store with ground-truth anchoring, disconfirmation filtering, held-out rollback, and anti-leakage retrieval. In scope as retained memory/playbook learning from execution feedback, compared with human-crafted experience.
mechanism: The task-level harness adds API retrieval, documentation responses, isolated sandbox execution, and static checking. Beyond single-task solving, governed self-evolution distills past traces into a three-tier memory store; updates are anchored to ground truth, filtered by disconfirmation, rolled back on a held-out set, and retrieved under an anti-leakage rule.
evaluation_signal: Authors report that the full task-level harness with self-evolution disabled reaches 92.4% pass@1 on the 158-task EDA-Eval-PyAether benchmark and outperforms ZhuLong on all five tested LLM backbones. On a harder instance-disjoint test set, self-evolution from the bare configuration is reported to reach 80.0% pass@1 versus 77.5% for a human-crafted-experience baseline.

title: Fix Where It Fails: Root-Cause-Guided Agentic Harness Optimization for Scene Graph Generation
why: RoHa-SGG extends agentic harness optimization to scene graph generation: it searches for inference-code edits around a frozen SGG model, guided by a root-cause analysis of where ground-truth triplets are lost, without retraining the model. In scope as scaffold/harness optimization from execution diagnostics.
mechanism: Two LLM agents act on the inference harness around a frozen SGG model: an RCA agent locates the components where triplets are lost and diagnoses why, and a proposer searches for a harness that addresses those causes. The model is not retrained.
evaluation_signal: Authors report improvements on every metric for all five model-dataset combinations on Visual Genome and PSG (two-stage, one-stage, and multimodal-LLM SGG models). Graph-constrained R@100 and mR@100 rise by up to 15.8 and 26.4 points for the multimodal LLM and by up to 3.6 and 10.1 points for the two-stage and one-stage models. Root-cause guidance is reported to reach the final score of an unguided search up to three times faster.

title: MedicalRSI: Medical Recursive Self-Improving Agents via Clinical Model-Harness Co-Evolution
why: An RSI framework in which one model plays Solver (the medical agent) and Improver (a learnable strategy that writes a medical harness from the agent's failures); each harness is rewarded by its gain over acting without it, and the Improver keeps adapting to unsolved problems. Harness writing is central, even though the two roles are trained together. Official repo description matches the paper title.
mechanism: Clinical Model-Harness Co-Evolution: the Improver writes a medical harness from Solver failures; each harness is scored by its gain over acting without it; both roles are trained together so the improving strategy itself keeps changing. The retained artifact used at inference is the written medical harness plus the updated roles.
evaluation_signal: Authors report that on multiple benchmarks and LLM backbones, MedicalRSI outperforms existing context-level and weight-level self-improvement methods and transfers to unseen workflows, new LLMs, and new databases. The abstract does not quote a single headline metric.

title: HyperHarness: Learning to Generate Personalized Agent Harnesses from User Histories
why: Learns a shared history-to-harness generator that synthesizes executable, user-specific retrieval and answer-guidance code from a user's history, without updating the answering model or running per-user scored search at deployment. In scope as amortized harness generation/optimization around frozen answering models.
mechanism: A construction LLM writes personalized retrieval and guidance functions from a user's permitted history. Downstream task scores across training users supervise iterative refinements of the shared generator (no reference harnesses; answering-model weights are not updated). At deployment the frozen generator builds a harness for each unseen user in a single pass.
evaluation_signal: Authors report results on PersonaMemv3, Mem-PAL, and MemoryCD with Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.8-27B, and GPT-5.6-Luna: HyperHarness achieves the highest aggregate score in seven of nine settings and ranks second in the other two, improving over the strongest baselines by up to 5.95 points and cutting matched answer-time tokens by 90.32% versus long-context prompting. Analyses are reported to show transfer to unseen user clusters.
